_comment: Skill Repo Spec v1 s9 -- every path in this repo belongs to exactly one class.
TOOL    = code, SKILL.md, docs, reference data, and metrics ABOUT THE SKILL. Public.
FIXTURE = LIFELIKE test data: rows that look like real records, whose real version is
sitting right there in the operator's life and is structurally indistinguishable.
Must be produced by tools/make_fixtures.py -- a real record cannot be regenerated,
so pasting one in fails at commit. (A self-evidently fake canary or an Acme mock is
NOT lifelike and does not need a generator; the risk it guards against is a person
reaching for a convenient REAL example, and there is no temptation to reach for a
real value that would look obviously wrong next to FAKE_CANARY_XYZ.)
DATA    = anything a REAL RUN produced. Never in a PUBLIC repo. Lives in the private companion
config, resolved at runtime by tools/datadir.py. This repo ships only the schema.
data_sealed = a path that HELD real data, was purged, and must stay dead.
Enforced by tools/data_boundary.py in .githooks and in CI.
`tool` is not a fourth class. It is the per-path allowlist for check 4, which fails any tracked
file that WEARS the shape of real-run output. TOOL is the default class and needs no entry --
except where a hand-written file is shaped like a ledger, which has to be argued for in the diff.
_tool_note: The former yield replay records are generated FIXTURE entries; no runtime-shaped record needs a TOOL exception.
_fixture_note: Every declared FIXTURE is reproduced by tools/make_fixtures.py. Source-provider names and category slugs describe parser contracts; identities, observations and histories are synthetic.
_fixture_backlog: Closed: all seven legacy source-parser and yield fixtures are generated by tools/make_fixtures.py, using invented identities and observations. Parser shape, routing, date, count and yield scenarios remain covered by their consumers.
_audited: Runtime source plans, pull and collection receipts, opportunities, digests, dedup state, roster consumption, source-health reports, completeness reports, wrapper logs and identity sweeps are DATA in the separate PRIVATE companion. Each write target is checked with Git and authenticated gh. Public, unknown, unversioned and own-tool targets fail closed. Reads may remain uninitialized; writers never invent a fallback.
_armed: Pinned guard tests and data-boundary checks remain required. The consumer adapter binds only its privately loaded resolver instance to the canonical repository root, including linked worktrees; pinned kit files remain unchanged.
_dependencies: Git and authenticated gh are required for writes. The pinned datadir resolver remains the discovery authority. A scoped consumer-root adapter handles its linked-worktree limitation; the shared-kit followup is recorded in private implementation evidence.
_data_home: DAILY_HOTSPOTS_CONFIG or DAILY_HOTSPOTS_DATA_DIR selects the companion through pinned guards. Explicit archive and roster destinations must also belong to a separately verified PRIVATE GitHub repository.
